reason: E1 and E2 support that mechanical alloying and SPS produce non-equilibrium nanocrystalline Mg–Ti–Zn alloys with enhanced corrosion resistance, but none of the cited evidence addresses the effects of post-sintering annealing at 300°C vs 600°C on grain boundary chemistry, oxide scale formation, or high-temperature oxidation behavior. The key premises about annealing-dependent microstructural evolution and its impact on protective oxide formation are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mechanical alloying and SPS produce a non-equilibrium, nanocrystalline Mg–Ti–Zn alloy with extended solid solubility
Low-temperature annealing (300°C) preserves this metastable nanocrystalline structure and Mg-enriched grain boundaries
High-temperature annealing (600°C) causes grain coarsening and formation of equilibrium intermetallic compounds
Preserved nanocrystalline structure with Mg-enriched boundaries promotes a protective oxide scale, improving corrosion and oxidation resistance
Coarsened/intermetallic-containing structure leads to poorer oxide adherence and worse corrosion/oxidation resistance
